source: read from the spell descriptions in content/spells/spells.json

effects.target: As zone of truth: the target cannot speak a deliberate lie while the spell lasts, and visibly takes on the semblance of a lawful outsider so onlookers know it is affected.

abadar-s-truthtelling.notes: Zone of truth's compulsion has no condition in the vocabulary; narrative. The visible guise is not a disguise (prose says it cannot pass as another race).

effects.target: Suppresses one curse afflicting the target for the duration. Does not restore damage or drain the curse caused, and cannot suppress curses remove curse cannot lift.

abeyance.notes: suppress_condition has no 'cursed' entry in the condition vocabulary, so this is narrative. Prose also caps it at one suppression per curse ever, which the vocabulary cannot express.

effects.target: Take two 5-foot steps each round, and cast spells or use spell-like abilities without provoking attacks of opportunity.
Discharges as soon as you attack, cast a harmful spell at a creature, or move more than 5 feet with a single move action.

abjuring-step.notes: Corpus duration is 'rounds/level (1) or until discharged'; the timed part is emitted and the discharge trigger is carried as a narrative spec since the shape has no trigger field.

effects.target: ac

effects.note: only against attacks that already deal nonlethal damage

effects.target: The first 5 points of lethal damage from each attack become nonlethal instead. After 5 points per caster level (maximum 50) have been converted, the spell discharges.

ablative-barrier.notes: Damage-type conversion has no vocabulary entry, so it is narrative. The DR 5/- is conditional on the attack being nonlethal, which the DR spec can only carry as a note.

effects.target: An immobile crystalline globe gives you improved cover. It is 1 inch thick per caster level, hardness 5, 3 hp per inch. At one-third hp lost it drops to cover, at two-thirds to partial cover, and at 0 hp it is destroyed. Spells' line of sight and effect pass through it freely.

ablative-sphere.notes: The prose's 'you take any remaining damage' is damage that leaks through the destroyed barrier from someone else's attack, not damage this spell deals - deliberately not converted to a damage spec.

effects.target: Breathe water freely.
The target can no longer breathe air while the spell lasts. Divide the duration evenly among every creature touched. No effect on creatures that already breathe water.

aboleth-s-lung.notes: The duration emitted is the total pool; the prose divides it between all targets, which the shape cannot express.

effects.target: Ends all charm and compulsion effects on the target as break enchantment, including harmless ones, and excuses any code-of-conduct breach committed while charmed. Automatic if caster and target share alignment or deity; 5% per caster level if their alignments are within one step; otherwise it fails.

absolution.notes: The 5%/level chance is a caster-level-scaled success roll, not damage scaling, so it stays in the narrative text rather than in `scaling`.

effects.target: Touch a magical rune, glyph or symbol and attempt a caster level check (DC 10 + the effect's caster level) to lift it onto a silk glove. Failure by 5 or more triggers the rune. Held inert on the glove, it can be transferred to a similar surface as a standard action, either working normally or dissipating, your choice. Affects only runes equivalent to a 3rd-level spell or lower; attempting a stronger one triggers it.

absorb-rune-i.notes: Corpus duration is 'instantaneous + minutes/level (1)'; the timed part (1 minute/caster level the rune stays inert) is what a buff clock needs, so that is what is emitted.

effects.target: As absorb rune I - touch a rune, make a caster level check (DC 10 + its caster level) to lift it onto a silk glove and later replace it elsewhere - but it affects runes equivalent to a 5th-level spell or lower.

As absorb rune I - touch a rune, make a caster level check (DC 10 + its caster level) to lift it onto a silk glove and later replace it elsewhere - but it affects runes equivalent to an 8th-level spell or lower.
disease you come into contact with
poison you come into contact with

When exposed to a disease or poison you may absorb it instead; that ends the immunity to everything except the absorbed affliction. While holding one you can transfer it with a melee touch attack (a miss does not discharge the spell); on a hit the spell discharges and the victim saves at this spell's DC or the affliction's, whichever is higher. If the duration expires first you are exposed to it yourself, with a +2 bonus on saves against that instance.

absorb-toxicity.notes: Recasting resets the duration rather than absorbing a second toxin - carried in prose only.

effects.note: against ranged weapons only; creatures and objects in the warded area

effects.target: Discharges once it has prevented 20 points of damage per caster level (maximum 200) across everything in the area. The area is shapeable and up to 40 feet high, so flying creatures inside it benefit.

Inhale one gas, fog, smoke or mist up to one 10-foot cube per level, removing it from the map (a magical cloud needs a caster level check, DC 11 + its caster level). Hold it inside, holding your breath, for up to 1 round per level, then exhale it as a standard action into a 60-foot cone or its original area, where it works normally against its original DC. Exhaling ends the spell; failing to exhale before it ends means you suffer the cloud's effects and automatically fail any save.

absorbing-inhalation.notes: No effect on gaseous creatures, and an instantaneous cloud such as a breath weapon needs a readied action.

effects.target: Absorb one nonmagical, nonliving object of up to 1 pound per caster level into your hand. It cannot be targeted while melded but still counts against your carry capacity; dismissing the spell returns it to that hand. One item per hand.

absorbing-touch.notes: An object in someone else's possession gets the Fortitude save the corpus already records.

effects.target: A handful of berries, grain, nuts or rice is enriched to feed a Medium or smaller creature for a full day. It creates no food, so it cannot by itself stop starvation.

abstemiousness.notes: The 1-hour duration is how long the enhancement lasts on the food, not how long the nourishment lasts - the corpus's own wording, not reinterpreted here.

effects.target: the spooked condition
Sense Motive checks to avoid surprise or to notice that a creature is threatening or malicious
initiative

50% chance to negate the shaken or scared condition from any source, including Intimidate demoralise, instead of gaining it. Other fear-derived effects (such as dying from phantasmal killer) work normally, and anything that ignores fear immunity ignores this too. Danger-sense effects such as anticipate peril still warn the target.

absurdity.notes: No bonus type is named for the -10 and -2, so both are untyped. 'Spooked' and 'scared' are not in the condition vocabulary; the immunity spec takes free text, the 50% chance does not fit any type.

effects.target: At the start of each round the warded quiver or pouch replaces nonmagical ammunition taken from it the round before, and the earlier ammunition vanishes. A later projectile-enhancing spell cast on the same container also affects everything this spell conjures.

abundant-ammunition.notes: Special materials, alchemical treatments and nonmagical coatings are not reproduced.

effects.target: Gives one vermin or vermin swarm the fiendish creature simple template: DR 5/good at 5+ HD or DR 10/good at 11+ HD, cold and fire resistance 5 at 5+ HD or 10 at 11+ HD, spell resistance equal to CR + 6, and smite good once per day (swift action, add Charisma bonus to attack and HD to damage against a good foe until it dies).

abyssal-vermin.notes: Every number here is gated on the target's Hit Dice. Emitting resistance or damage_reduction specs would apply the 5+ HD numbers to a weaker vermin that should get nothing, so the whole template stays narrative. A vermin under your command auto-fails its save.

effects.target: Hastens a poison already in the target: an onset time is skipped and it takes effect immediately, or if it has no onset its frequency doubles (two saves and two intervals of damage per round or minute) while its duration halves. The cure condition is unchanged.

accelerate-poison.notes: This spell inflicts no damage of its own; the doubled damage is the existing poison's.

effects.target: Move an affliction - curse, disease or poison - or one of the blinded, deafened, fatigued, nauseated, shaken or sickened conditions off the touched creature and onto yourself. Save DCs, remaining duration and removal conditions carry over unchanged, now applying to you.

accept-affliction.notes: Left narrative on purpose: remove_condition names one fixed condition, but which affliction moves is chosen at casting, and the vocabulary has no way to say the caster then gains it.

effects.target: The cursed creature rolls twice and takes the lower result on every attack roll and saving throw for the duration.

While you cast, each ally within range of the subject may attempt an Intimidate check as a move action (DC equal to this spell's save DC); each success gives you a cumulative +2 on your caster level check to beat spell resistance.

accursed-glare.notes: Roll-twice-take-lower has no spec type - it is not a numeric penalty, so no combat_mod or save_mod could state it without inventing a number.

effects.note: requires a ranged touch attack to hit; no splash damage

effects.target: Unless neutralised the acid keeps burning, dealing another 2d4 acid damage each round for one extra round per three caster levels, to a maximum of 6 extra rounds at 18th level.

acid-arrow.notes: Corpus duration is 'rounds (1) + rounds/3 levels (1)' and the shape cannot add a per-level term to a fixed one, so the base round is emitted and the extension named in the narrative spec. The repeating 2d4 is deliberately not a second damage spec: the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type. No `scaling` - the caster level buys rounds, not dice.

effects.target: A 20-foot-radius, 20-foot-high bank of acidic vapour, as solid fog: it obscures sight and slows movement to a crawl. Each round on your turn, starting the round you cast it, the fog deals 2d6 acid damage to every creature and object inside it.

acid-fog.notes: The 2d6 repeats every round for the whole duration and the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type, so it is not emitted as a damage spec. There is no save and no SR.

effects.target: The target animal companion's bite attack deals an extra 1d4 acid damage, and the acid deals a further 1d4 to whatever it bit on the following round, continuing for 1 extra round per 4 caster levels (6 rounds total at caster level 20th). Ongoing acid from multiple bites does not stack, but a newer bite resets the remaining duration if it would be longer. The acid never harms the companion.

acid-maw.notes: Not a damage spec: the spell targets the animal companion, who takes none of this damage - it lands on whatever the companion bites, and it repeats each round.

effects.target: As create pit, but with a 5-foot-deep pool of acid at the bottom; the pit is 10 feet by 10 feet and 10 feet deep per two caster levels, to a maximum of 100 feet. A creature that falls in takes normal falling damage (the acid counts as a yielding surface) plus 2d6 acid damage per round in contact with the acid. Exposed carried items are attacked one at a time per Table 9-2 and must save after 3 consecutive rounds or gain the broken condition; broken objects must save each round or be destroyed. The walls have a Climb DC of 30.

acid-pit.notes: The 2d6 is per round of contact - repeating damage, so not a damage spec. Falling damage is the fall's, not the spell's. Corpus duration is 'rounds (1) + rounds/level (1)'; the shape cannot add a fixed round to a per-level term, so the per-level term is emitted and the extra opening round is noted here.

effects.target: perception
effects.note: rises to +20 at caster level 8th and +30 (the maximum) at caster level 16th

acute-senses.notes: No `scaling` emitted: the progression steps at caster levels 8 and 16, which the scaling shape (a per-level increment) cannot express without inventing a rate.

effects.target: Your blood sets like glue on contact with air. Any piercing or slashing weapon that deals you hit point damage sticks fast unless its wielder makes a Reflex save; prying a stuck weapon free is a standard action and a Strength check against the spell's DC. Strong alcohol or universal solvent dissolves it. The glue fails underwater or anywhere without air, and breaks down when the spell ends or 5 rounds after you die.

adhesive-blood.notes: The Reflex save belongs to whoever strikes you, not to you, so no save_gate wraps this - it does not gate the buff landing.

effects.target: Once during the duration, spit adhesive at a creature within 15 feet as a standard action with no attack roll needed; it functions as a tanglefoot bag, except every DC to resist it - avoiding being stuck to the floor, staying aloft, breaking free, casting a spell - uses this spell's save DC. The adhesive lasts 2d4 rounds after it lands, and spitting discharges the spell.

adhesive-spittle.notes: Left narrative rather than apply_condition entangled: the prose says only 'functions as a tanglefoot bag' and never names a condition, and a tanglefoot bag's result varies with the target's save.

effects.target: As disguise self, but you can change the illusory appearance as a swift action, within disguise self's limits, a number of times equal to your caster level.
As alter self, but you can change your form as a swift action, within alter self's limits, a number of times equal to your caster level.
diplomacy
effects.note: only while out of combat, on checks to influence creatures

effects.target: performance combat checks

adoration.notes: The two +2s are alternatives, not cumulative - the prose gives the Diplomacy bonus out of combat and the performance combat bonus in it.

effects.target: Draw a stored item weighing less than 1 pound per caster level (maximum 15 pounds) either as a move action that does not provoke, or as a swift action that does.
fort

Strength-based and Dexterity-based checks
Any bleed effect on the target deals +1 point of damage, and the target heals naturally at half the normal rate.

advanced-scurvy.notes: Instantaneous casting, but the disease it inflicts persists until cured; proper nutrition ends the fatigue and bone pain in 1-2 days and cures it fully 2d6 days after that. No hit point damage anywhere in the prose.

effects.target: Air within 100 feet + 10 feet per level of you ripples and glows where creatures flew through it in the last day per caster level, lit well enough to follow without lighting penalties. The area travels with you, so you can follow the trail from the air or from the ground below it, and anyone moving with you can follow it too. Survival DCs to track through the air match tracking across soft ground.

As lesser age resistance, but you ignore the Strength, Dexterity and Constitution penalties from both middle age and old age. Age-related mental bonuses are kept, you do not look younger, and you can still die of old age.

age-resistance.notes: Not emitted as ability_mod specs: this cancels penalties a character only has if aged, so a flat bonus would be plain wrong on a young caster, and the old-age penalty sizes are never stated in this text.

effects.target: As lesser age resistance, but you ignore every Strength, Dexterity and Constitution penalty from middle age, old age and venerable age. Age-related mental bonuses are kept, you do not look younger, and you can still die of old age.

age-resistance-greater.notes: Same reasoning as age resistance: cancelling an age penalty is not a bonus and the penalty sizes are not stated here.

effects.target: You ignore the -1 penalties to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution that middle age imposes, while keeping the age-related bonuses to Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma. Penalties from old or venerable age still apply in full. You do not look younger and can still die of old age.

age-resistance-lesser.notes: The -1s are stated, but they are penalties this spell cancels only if the caster is middle-aged; emitting +1 ability_mods would hand a bonus to a young caster who never had the penalty.

effects.target: Every recurring affliction on the target - curse, disease or poison with a frequency - triggers at once, forcing an immediate save against each as that affliction describes. A success does not count toward shaking the affliction off and the next scheduled save is unchanged. Afflictions with no frequency are unaffected.

aggravate-affliction.notes: The saves are the afflictions' own, at their own DCs, so no save_gate: this spell's 'see text' save is those.

effects.target: A conjured outsider or elemental that fails a Fortitude save takes a -1 penalty per two caster levels (maximum -10) on all saves and checks made against you for the next hour, and any creature demanding payment for its service cuts that payment by 20% per four caster levels (maximum 60%). The tortured creature resents you and is likelier to twist your orders or seek revenge later. No effect on creatures immune to nonlethal damage.

agonize.notes: The penalty is -1 per 2 caster levels, which no spec can hold: situational_mod takes a single fixed amount, and writing -1 there would be wrong at every caster level above 3. The corpus duration is 1 round but the penalty the prose imposes lasts an hour.

effects.target: attack
will
effects.note: against fear effects
1d8 + caster level, to a maximum of 1d8+10 at caster level 10th

aid.notes: The save bonus is written 'saves against fear effects'; recorded on Will with a note, matching how the already-converted bless entry states the same clause.

effects.target: Breathe air freely.
Divide the duration evenly among every creature touched. The targets do not lose the ability to breathe water.

air-breathing.notes: Targets aquatic creatures; the duration emitted is the total pool before it is divided among them.

effects.target: Breathe underwater or in an airless environment, from a pocket of air around your head.

Cast on an object instead, it shields that object from water damage. A firearm inside the bubble can be loaded from an airtight source and fired; shots underwater still take -2 on the attack roll per 5 feet of water crossed, and an exploding firearm explodes normally.

Creatures you try to pull rank on treat you as their own direct superior unless they make a Will save to disbelieve. Different creatures picture a different superior, and the contradictions that produces can earn them extra saves.
Walk on air up to 1 foot off the ground: ignore difficult terrain lower than 1 foot and set off nothing that triggers on weight, such as a pressure plate. You cannot cross liquid.

effects.note: to a minimum of 5 feet; not reduced at all if you have 1 rank in Fly

effects.note: not taken if you have 5 ranks in Fly

effects.note: not taken if you have 5 ranks in Fly

effects.note: not taken if you have 5 ranks in Fly

effects.target: Anyone trying to track you across ground you crossed this way takes -10 on the Perception or Survival check. With 1 rank in Fly you can also cross liquid at half speed; with 5 ranks, at full speed.

air-step.notes: No bonus type is named for the -4s, so they are untyped. The speed and skill penalties are the default case; the Fly-rank exemptions are carried as notes because the spec has no condition field. The -10 falls on the tracker, not on the caster, so it is narrative rather than a skill_mod.

effects.target: Tread on air as though it were solid ground, climbing or descending at up to a 45-degree angle at half your normal speed.

A wind of 21+ mph pushes the air walker 5 feet at the end of each of its turns per 5 mph of wind speed, with worse consequences in violent or turbulent air. When the spell ends or is dispelled while you are aloft you float down 60 feet per round for 1d6 rounds, landing safely if you reach the ground in that time and falling the rest of the way if not - an antimagic field instead drops you outright. A mount can be trained to move under air walk with a week's work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check.

air-walk.notes: Not a fly speed: the prose gives ground-walking on air at half speed on slopes, not manoeuvrable flight, so no speed spec. The 1d6 per 10 feet is ordinary falling damage after the magic fails, not damage this spell deals.

effects.target: Tread on air as though it were solid ground, climbing or descending at up to a 45-degree angle at half your normal speed.
As air walk, except the duration is split in 10-minute intervals among every creature touched.

air-walk-communal.notes: Duration emitted is the total pool before it is divided among the targets.

effects.target: Knowledge checks made through this spell

Attempt one Knowledge check of your choice per three caster levels, counting as trained in each, including rerolls of Knowledge checks you have already failed. The GM rolls them in secret; a natural 1 returns a wildly wrong answer. Dawdling, discussing the answers or doing anything else ends the spell, and you cannot consult the Record about the same topic again until you gain a caster level.

akashic-communion.notes: The +10 is stated as an insight bonus and applies only to the checks this spell buys, hence situational_mod rather than a blanket skill_mod on every Knowledge skill.

effects.target: Stores a snapshot of your body - hit points, physical ability scores, and physical conditions such as ability damage, disease, negative levels and poison - in the Akashic Record. If you drop below 0 hit points or are killed by a non-mind-affecting death effect while the spell lasts, you may let the body die and take up the stored record on your next turn: the corpse vanishes and you reappear in its place wearing whatever clothing was still on it, or anywhere you have been within 500 feet of the corpse with no gear at all. Your mind is unchanged, so no spells return; mental influences and energy drain carry over, but physical afflictions acquired since casting do not. It cannot dodge death by old age, and recasting overwrites the stored copy.

Wards a 20-foot-radius area so that any Tiny or larger creature entering or touching it trips an alarm, unless it speaks the password you chose at casting. You choose mental or audible when you cast. Mental alerts only you, anywhere within a mile, as a single ping that wakes you from normal sleep without breaking concentration, and silence does not stop it. Audible rings like a hand bell for 1 round, clear within 60 feet, less 10 feet per closed door and 20 feet per substantial wall, faintly audible up to 180 feet in quiet, and inaudible inside a silence spell. Ethereal and astral creatures never trip it. Permanency can make it permanent.

on_failure.target: A permanent curse like burn spellblight: each time the victim casts a spell or uses a spell-like ability its skin seems to burn, wreathed in visible violet flame. A concentration check (DC 15 + twice the spell's level) ignores the pain; on a failure the spell or slot is lost and the caster is staggered for 1 round.

alaznist-s-jinx.notes: The staggered condition is not emitted as apply_condition: it only lands when the victim later fails a concentration check, not when the spell is cast.

effects.target: If you drink a potion or elixir on the round after taking this extract, you gain its full benefit and then spit it back into its container as a free action, so it is not used up. One potion or elixir per use.

Turns one alchemical item or firearm into a different alchemical item or firearm of equal or lower cost. Magic items are immune. When the spell ends, an alchemical item that was used while transformed is destroyed rather than restored, and a firearm reverts to its original type.

alchemical-tinkering.notes: The Fortitude save is an object save for an item someone else holds, not a gate on the transformation the caster performs on their own gear, so no save_gate.

effects.target: land
effects.note: enhancement bonus; does not stack with haste or similar effects

effects.target: ac
effects.note: does not stack with haste or similar effects

effects.target: Take 5-foot steps in difficult terrain.

aldori-alacrity.notes: The speed bonus is stated as an enhancement bonus; the speed spec has no bonus_type field, so it is recorded in the note.

effects.target: Makes one weapon, or 50 projectiles gathered together, chaotic, evil, good or lawful as you choose, letting it bypass damage reduction keyed to that alignment. No effect on a weapon that already has an alignment, and it cannot be cast on a natural weapon such as an unarmed strike. The spell itself takes the alignment descriptor you choose.

As align weapon, but the duration is divided in 1-minute increments among any number of touched weapons; each group of up to 50 projectiles gathered together at casting counts as one weapon for the split.

align-weapon-communal.notes: Duration emitted is the total pool before it is divided.

effects.target: haste
effects.note: you gain haste's benefits for as long as you keep the bardic performance going

effects.target: You must already be maintaining a bardic performance to cast it, and the spell ends the moment that performance stops or is interrupted. As an immediate action you can dismiss it to reroll a Reflex save or a Dexterity-based skill check, declared before the first result is known, and you must keep the reroll even if it is worse. It dispels and is dispelled by slow.

allegro.notes: Haste's numbers are deliberately not copied in - the prose grants 'the benefits of the spell haste', so spell_effect names the spell rather than restating figures that would then need keeping level with haste's own entry.

effects.target: the effects of addiction
If the subject rests for the whole duration, she recovers naturally from damage the drug dealt.

Choose one use at casting. Combat Corruption lowers the target's corruption stage by 1 (nothing if it is not already at stage 1 or higher). Remove Corruption strips one manifestation level plus the most recent manifestation with its gift and stain, weakening anything that scales with manifestation level; losing every manifestation level cures the corruption. Either use needs a caster level check against DC 10 + twice the manifestation level + three times the corruption stage. Fail by 5 or more and you contract the corruption yourself and gain a manifestation - or, if you already have it, save against it immediately. A natural 1 always fails. Casting it on yourself, or on someone who has fully succumbed, always fails, and no creature can benefit more than once a week.

Turns one object of up to 5 pounds per caster level into a bland, gooey but edible substance any living creature can digest; one pound feeds a Medium creature for a day. Similar objects piled together count as one object. Magical or otherwise exceptional objects cannot be transformed. The object's hardness counts as 0 for eating it but is unchanged against sundering or breaking.

allfood.notes: The prose's 'takes damage accordingly' is what happens to someone who eats a transformed burning torch - the torch's damage, not this spell's, so no damage spec.

effects.target: ac

Once each round on your turn you can direct the animated garment as a free action to use aid another on your skill check, attack roll or AC. Its attack bonus or total skill bonus equals your caster level plus your key spellcasting ability modifier. If someone else puts the cloak on, it protects and aids that wearer but still uses your bonus. It can take no other action.

on_failure.target: The enemy is drawn to you and must spend its move action at the start of each of its turns closing on you by the most direct route, stepping around obstacles but never into something obviously harmful such as a pit, caltrops or a wall of fire. Losing sight of you suspends the compulsion and regaining sight renews it. Any hostile action against the creature, including an attack of opportunity provoked by its own movement, breaks the effect on it.

effects.target: The opening flash raises the light level in the area by one step, up to normal light, for 1 round per caster level - darkness becomes dim, dim becomes normal.

alluring-light.notes: The corpus records the duration as instantaneous, but the prose states both effects last 1 round per caster level, so that is what is emitted. Compelled movement has no condition in the vocabulary.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: saving throws against the caster's enchantment spells and effects
The penalty is -2 instead for any creature that is, or could be, sexually attracted to the caster.

alluring-spores.notes: No bonus type is stated for the penalty, so untyped. The -2 variant depends on a fact about the creature, which no spec field can test.

effects.target: Creates one 5-foot cube of temporal possibility per two caster levels within range. As a free action you can call a duplicate of yourself into a cube you can see; it lasts until the end of your turn, uses your statistics but has hit points equal to your caster level, threatens adjacent squares and shares your teamwork feats. It appears with copies of your gear but cannot use any of it, and the gear vanishes with it. It cannot leave its square and can only use aid another once, nothing else. Its cube dissipates when it goes. You get one duplicate, plus one more per 4 caster levels beyond 3rd, but never two at once.
handle animal

Animals treat you as a social superior: the starting attitude of any animal you deal with improves one step. Helpful animals give simple assistance such as aid another on checks they understand, but flee from attacks and will not fight for you. Once during the duration you can silently command helpful animals within 60 feet to forage; an hour later they return to that spot with enough food for one meal for you and a number of others equal to your caster level.

One instrument sounds like a different kind of instrument you know, from a small change to a drastic one. Volume, pitch range and how it is played are all unchanged, so a piccolo made to sound like an organ is still piccolo-loud, still high-pitched and still a wind instrument.

Choose one use. Alter Current speeds or slows a natural freshwater channel by up to 1 mile per hour per two caster levels, changing how far it carries creatures downstream each round and the Swim DC to match. Divert River sends the river in a direction you choose, following the local terrain, never uphill; it bursts its banks and floods lower ground, and creatures in its path risk being swept away. Permanency can make either use permanent.

alter-river.notes: The mile-per-hour figures in the prose are reference values for river speeds, not a change this spell applies on its own.

effects.target: Assume the form of any Small or Medium creature of the humanoid type.

If the chosen form has them you gain darkvision 60 feet, low-light vision, scent and a swim speed of 30 feet. A Small humanoid form gives a +2 size bonus to Dexterity; a Medium humanoid form gives a +2 size bonus to Strength instead.

alter-self.notes: The two +2 size bonuses are alternatives chosen when the form is picked, so emitting both as ability_mod specs would hand out +2 Str and +2 Dex at once. The senses are likewise conditional on the form actually having them, so no sense specs.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Swap a summoned creature for one you could call with summon monster or summon nature's ally of the same level or lower than the spell that summoned it, provided the environment can support the new creature. The original summoning's duration is untouched and other creatures from that same casting are unaffected. The replacement arrives with the same damage and conditions, and stays subject to any curses, diseases, poisons and penalties on the original, but no other spells carry over.

alter-summoned-monster.notes: A summoned creature under your control gets no save. Eidolons cannot be targeted. The spell takes the alignment descriptors of the creature swapped in.

effects.target: Within an immobile 10-foot-radius emanation around a point you touch, natural wind is raised or lowered one step in intensity. The strongest wind you can affect depends on caster level: light at 1st-3rd, moderate at 4th-9th, strong at 10th-15th, severe at 16th and above. Magical winds are unaffected.

alter-winds.notes: The Will save the corpus records has no creature target here - the spell affects an area of weather - so it is not wrapped in a save_gate.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target loses access to almost all memory: it forgets its past, its name and its training, losing every class ability, feat and skill rank it had, though it keeps its languages, base attack bonus, saves, CMB, CMD, experience, Hit Dice and hit points and can still perform basic tasks. New levels work normally, but a level in a class it already had is used as a 1st-level character of that class until the amnesia is cured, at which point everything returns. Only heal, limited wish, miracle, psychic surgery or wish can lift it.

effects.target: Every potion or elixir you drink for the duration counts as empowered: all its variable numeric effects increase by half. Its attack bonus is your caster level plus your Intelligence or Charisma bonus, plus another +1 per four caster levels (maximum +5 at 20th). It hits for 4d10 with a x4 critical modifier. AC 10, hardness 10, 80 hit points, uses your saving throw modifiers, never provokes. Destroying it destroys your focus.

arcane-cannon.notes: The 4d10 is not emitted as a damage spec: it is the cannon's attack against whatever it shoots, resolved on an attack roll, not damage this spell applies to a target.

effects.target: A 10-foot radiance around you enhances arcane spells cast by anyone inside it: each gains a +1 enhancement bonus to the DC of saves made against it, and is cast as though one metamagic feat - Enlarge Spell, Extend Spell, Silent Spell or Still Spell, chosen when you cast this spell - had been applied, with no increase to spell level or casting time.

arcane-concordance.notes: The +1 raises the save DC of somebody else's spell. save_mod moves a creature's saving throw, not a spell's DC, so it would say the opposite of what the prose means.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The subject must succeed at a concentration check (DC 10 + half its caster level) to cast any arcane spell, use any spell-like ability even a divine one, use arcane spell completion or spell trigger items, or use arcane school powers, arcanist exploits, bardic performances, magus arcana or witch hexes. Anything taking a free, swift or immediate action is exempt, as are mythic spells and mythic power. On top of that, any concentration check it must make for another reason - casting defensively, being injured mid-cast - takes a penalty equal to half its caster level.

arcane-disruption.notes: The concentration DC and the extra penalty both scale off the subject's own caster level, so no fixed-amount spec could hold either.

effects.target: An invisible sensor forms at any point you can see and then travels freely out of your sight, feeding you exactly what you would see standing there. It moves 30 feet a round scanning ahead as a human would, or 10 feet a round if it also examines walls and ceilings, in any direction for the duration. Solid barriers stop it, but it slips through any hole an inch across, and it cannot leave the plane even through a gate. You must concentrate to use it; without concentration it sits inert until you resume.

Magically locks a door, chest or portal of up to 30 square feet per level; you pass your own arcane lock freely without disturbing it. An existing lock's DC to open rises by 10 while it stays attached; an object with no lock gains one that needs a DC 20 Disable Device check. Add 10 to the DC to break the object open. Only breaking in, dispel magic or knock gets past it, and knock merely suppresses it for 10 minutes rather than removing it.

Inscribe your personal rune or mark of up to six characters, visible or invisible, on any substance without harming it. Detect magic makes an invisible mark glow, though not necessarily readable; see invisibility, true seeing, a gem of seeing or a robe of eyes also reveal it, and read magic reads any words. It cannot be dispelled but you or an erase spell can remove it, and on a living creature it fades over about a month. An object must be marked this way before instant summons can be cast on it.
